steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Chief, everything is ready. Anne has agreed to commence the contamination cleanup at any time.
Considering the safety of the areas around Syndicate, the MBCC has removed all the immersion tanks from SALVA.
At the moment, hundreds of Corruptor remains slumber in the blue potion in front of you.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Anne said she didn't want to do it herself, but she told me how to open the immersion tank. She also left you a notebook.
After the interrogation, you returned the notebook to its original owner. Now, it is in your hands again.
Why did she give this to me?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: My job is just giving it to you.
You open the familiar notebook and discover some changes.
A new "wish" has been added to the records of each immersion tank.
"Return to Eastside to be with my wife"... "Make a name for myself in a gang"... "Become a singer"... "Teach my son to read"...
Anne recalled the wishes of each patient. She didn't forget to add Gary's wish of "Visiting Eastside for fun" and Paige's wish to "be with Anne."
You browse through these newly added annotations and find a letter in the middle of the notebook.
You open the letter. The handwriting is neat and graceful, and the paper seems to be tinged with the tranquil fragrance of the notebook's owner.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Dear Chief, hope this letter finds you well.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I haven't gone out for so many days. I must have worried you.

By the time you read this letter, the FAC's contamination cleanup may have already begun.
In the face of death, I show more fear than a child. Although you don't say it directly, in your heart you may have secretly blamed me...
I'm sorry that my naive persistence has brought you a lot of trouble.

The notion of "back from the dead" is just a selfish lie to appease my own guilt. I've not only deceived my patients, but also deceived myself.
While I thought I can store them in the immersion tanks, I failed to realize that their reasons for living were never simply to stay "alive."
They are still alive in my memory, and shall stay there for the rest of my life.
I will do what I can to fulfill their wishes.

As the only survivor of the prevention and control site and a SALVA Hospital nurse, there is another thing I need to complete.
Continue Syndrome Mania research.
Sinners usually experience enormous mental stress during the incubation period after their infection. Their abilities are awakened at the same time as their will to fight, and their mutation also stagnates at this time... I think this is by no means a mere coincidence. It may hold the key to curing Mania.

I volunteer as a Sinner test subject to facilitate the FAC's research.
This is not only for my past patients, but also for those in Syndicate who have not yet been affected. As long as we can cure Syndrome Mania, I am willing to try.
Even if there is only a tiny sliver of hope.
Head Nurse of SALVA Hospital, MBCC Sinner, Anne, N.F. 112.
Each pen stroke extends gently across the thin pages, yet in your hands they feel like a thousand kilos.
When you look back at the annotations in the notebook, you can almost see from the circles what Anne looked like when she was writing them.
She locked herself in the room and tried to recall all the moments she shared with the deceased patients, and the experiences they told her.
Anne got to know each patient like her own family and friends. While analyzing the will to live, she also forced herself to return to the empty hospital beds.
You look up from the letter. Hecate still stands before you, awaiting your next order.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Alright... Chief, are you going to watch?

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: The scene may cause you discomfort.
Then do you know where Anne is? She's probably not feeling well either. I'll go take a look.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: After she gave me these things, she went out alone.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: No, she said she couldn't bear to watch, and then left alone.
Then please handle everything according to procedure. I'm going to see her.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Okay.
You find Anne in a secluded corner of the Bureau.
Anne sits quietly under a canopy of stars, gazing up at the night sky without looking back.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Chief, the weather is nice tonight.

options: How did you know it was me?

choices.text: How did you know it was me?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: People's footsteps are different.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Iron's footsteps are always in a hurry. She has a clear purpose and will not stop for anything.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Victoria's footsteps are light and airy. She doesn't know where she's going, but she's curious about the things around her and always walks slowly.
What about mine?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Chief, your footsteps are gentle and won't disturb others. But they are also very firm... Every step is thought out, and knows its direction.

options: You like to observe these things?

choices.text: You like to observe these things?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: It's part of my job to observe carefully and identify the needs of doctors and patients before they realize themselves.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: From what I know about you, I guess you're here to comfort me, right?
You're right.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Don't worry, I'm fine.
She gently points to her heart.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: These days, I already bid them farewell here.
She smiles in relief.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Thank you, Chief.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: From saving the girl in SALVA, to letting go of Gary, to now keeping me company, you have done so much for me. Yet I have nothing to repay you with.
That's not true!

options: You can repay me with work.
You can repay me with yourself.

choices.text: You can repay me with work.
You can repay me with yourself.

steps.content: The nurses from the MBCC medical department come to my office every day to ask "Why hasn't Anne come back to work?"... "Why did Anne lock herself up?"... "Chief, if you mistreat Anne, the entire medical department will not spare you"...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Pfff...
Why are you laughing?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Chief, you're adorable when you imitate how others talk.
Really...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Oh my, Chief, you're blushing!

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Eh? Chief, you want me to give myself to you?
You think I'm that corrupt?!
I'm saying that the MBCC needs you! The medical staff are all waiting for you to go back and help!

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Oh, is that so?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Chief, what are you blushing for?
...I'm not!

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Hahahaha... alright.
Anne flashes a rare relaxed smile. Usually, her smiles are of a professional nature.
Since you've known her, there have been two huge weights on her chest. One was the expectations of patients, and the other was the guilt of a healthcare worker.
Boom—
A loud noise echoes from the depot, and a strange fragrance wafts in from the distance.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: It's the smell of potion that stores remains... seems like Hecate is finished.
Neither of you speak. You simply sit side by side amidst the fragrance, quietly gazing at the night sky.
Suddenly, a white light flashes across the sky.
Anne, it's a meteor.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: No, that's...
Anne's voice chokes with joy.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: That's Paige.
